instruction.text: George loves painting. He uses 7/9 of a bottle of paint per painting. How many bottles of paint does George need to paint 9 paintings?

atoms.a: Calculate the number of bottles as a fraction.
Write the answer as a number.

atoms.b: George needs <mat><gap>7</gap></mat> bottles of paint to finish 9 paintings.

instruction.text: Chandra is running for charity. One lap is 4/5 of a kilometre. Chandra ends up running 7 laps. How many kilometres did she run?

atoms.a: Calculate the number of kilometres as a fraction.
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.

instruction.text: Mohammed is baking batches of cookies. Each batch of cookies needs 3/11 of a bag of flour. How much flour does Theo need if he wants to bake 6 batches of cookies?

atoms.a: Calculate the amount of bags of flour as a fraction.
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.

instruction.text: Mohammed now plans to bake <t-blue>10</t-blue> batches of cookies. He has 2 bags of flour. Does Mohammed have enough flour?

atoms.a: Calculate the amount of bags of flour as a fraction.
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.

atoms.b: Mohammed ((has ++doesn’t_have)) enough flour to make 10 batches of cookies.

instruction.text: Jacky has 7 chocolate bars. Each of her 3 friends want 3/4 of a chocolate bar. How many chocolate bars does Jacky need to give to her friends?

atoms.a: Calculate the amount of chocolate bars she needs to give away as a fraction.
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.

instruction.text: Could Jacky give each of her friends 3/4 of a chocolate bar if she had 9 friends?

atoms.a: Calculate the amount of chocolate bars she would need to give away as a fraction.
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.

atoms.b: Jacky ((wouldn’t ++would)) be able to give 9 of her friends each <mat><t-yellow>3</t-yellow>/<t-purple>4</t-purple></mat> of a chocolate bar.

instruction.text: Anna walks 8/13 of a kilometre to school each day.

atoms.a: How many kilometres has Anna walked after <t-blue>7</t-blue> days?
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.
How many kilometres has Anna walked after a <t-blue>month</t-blue>?
Convert the fraction into a mixed number.
